characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.value:
PVT was defined as "the development of two or more of the following: pain, erythema, swelling, excessive warmth or a palpable venous cord". However, in the discussion, the trial author stated that "even a small area of erythema was recorded as phlebitis" (i.e. only 1 sign).

It is unclear what proportion of participants were on continuous infusion.

Catheters were inserted "at the instruction of the principal investigator".

"All patients were reviewed daily by the principal investigator, and examined for signs of PVT at the current and all previous infusion sites".

references.title: Routine replacement versus replacement as clinical indicated of peripheral intravenous catheters: a multisite randomised controlled trial

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value:
Clinically indicated: Patients in the clinically indicated group continued to have PVCs until they showed any of the following signs: phlebitis, infiltration, occlusion, displacement, local infection, or a confirmed PVC-related bloodstream infection.

Routine removal: Patients in the routine removal group had their PVCs taken out every 96 hours. Catheters were also removed if any clinical indications arose within 4 days, following standard practice.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.value: Author contacted for results for patients without administration of TPN

characteristics.name: Outcomes
characteristics.value:
Critical Outcomes

CRBSI: defined as "(1) there is at least one positive blood culture from a peripheral vein; (2) there are clinical signs of infection (i.e. fever with body temperature >38.5°C, hypothermia with body temperature <36.5°C, chills or hypotension (systolic blood pressure <90 mmHg)); (3) there is no other apparent source of the bloodstream infection except the intravenous catheter which is in situ within 48 hours of the bloodstream infection; and (4) the culture of intravascular catheter tip shows at least 1000 cfu/mL with the same organism (same species)  as identified in blood." 

Primary BSI: defined as "any positive blood culture drawn from a peripheral vein while the PVC is in situ or 48 hours after removal." 

Local Infection: defined as "there are organisms grown from purulent discharge with no evidence of associated bloodstream infection." 

Mortality: Reported

Important Outcomes

Thrombophlebitis: defined as "phlebitis classification definition recommended by the American Infusion Nurses Society which in-cludes grade 0 to 4."

Infiltration: defined as " leaking of non-blistering drug from the vein of the infusion and resulting in swelling around the insertion site."

Catheter occlusion: defined as "the infusion does not drip, and flushing with normal saline is unsuccessful."

Limited Importance

Cost: the total cost of supplies for PVC insertion and maintenance (did not include labour)

Pain: Not included

Satisfaction: Not included

Catheters per participant: Reported - median (IQR)

Other outcomes reported in trial

Catheter failure: Reported

Displacement: defined as "the accidental catheter removal."

Catheter dwell time: Reported - cumulative - median (IQR)

characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
Country: China

Number: A total of 3,050 patients eligible for IV therapy were randomised into two groups across three participating hospitals, which used a total of 4572 catheters. Of these, 1,556 patients were placed in the clinically indicated removal group, while 1494 patients were in the routine removal group. After removal of patients who received TPN, 1477 patients were included in the clinically indicated group, and 1410 in the routine removal group.

Age: Clinically indicated group: 58.66 years  ± 15.89; routine removal 59.23 years ± 15.80

Sex (M/F): Clinically indicated group: 869/606; routine removal: 818/592

Inclusion criteria: Participants were aged over 18 years, able to provide written consent either themselves or via their nominated representative, and had a peripheral intravenous catheter in place with an expected intravenous therapy duration exceeding four days.

Exclusion criteria: Current BSI patients had a planned catheter removal within 24 hours, had PVC in place for more than 72 hours at screening, or had an immunodeficiency disease or were on immunosuppressive therapy.

characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
Country: China

Number: A total of 600 participants were recruited from various departments, including hepatobiliary and pancreatic surgery, orthopaedics, gastroenterology, neurology, cardiovascular medicine, neurosurgery, nephrology, thoracic surgery, and urology. Each department contributed 60 participants, with 30 assigned to clinically indicated procedures and 30 to routine removals. This resulted in 300 participants in the clinically indicated group and 30 in the routine removal group. 

Age: clinically indicated 56.34 years (16.27); routine removal 58.68 years (14.37)

Sex (M/F): clinically indicated 196/104; routine removal 199/101 

Inclusion criteria: Individuals aged 18 years or older, during hospitalisation, had their first use of a PVC in the limb, with an anticipated indwelling duration exceeding 96 hours, and written informed consent was duly obtained. 

Exclusion criteria: "infusion of corrosive drugs,  a history of thrombotic diseases, lower extremity catheterisation, scratches and burns on the local part of the catheter, changes in the plan of infusion therapy and a dwelling time of PVC of less than 96 hours, and not using PVC infusion for more than 24 hours."

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value:
Routine removal: "the catheter was removed in the routine replacement group: (i)  if clinically indicated symptoms presented within 96 hours. (ii) The catheter is removed regularly every 96 hours."

Clinically indicated:  "The catheter was removed in the clinically indicated group if any of the following criteria were met. 

(i) Signs and symptoms of complications with or without infusion through the catheter include but are not limited to the presence of any level of pain and/or tenderness with or without palpation, changes in color (erythema or blanching), changes in skin temperature (hot or cold), edema, induration, leakage of fluid or purulent drainage from the insertion site, and other types of dysfunction (e.g. resistance when flushing, absence of a blood return). 

(ii) The infusion therapy was completed."

characteristics.name: Outcomes
characteristics.value:
Critical outcomes

CRBSI: defined as "bacteremia or fungal blood during catheter insertion and within 48 hours after catheter removal, accompanied by fever (>38°C), chills, hypotension, and other infection manifestations, with no other source of infection except blood vessels."

Primary BSI: Not included

Local Infection: defined as "may include but is not limited to, erythema extending at least 1 cm from the insertion site, induration at the exit site or over the pocket, the exudate from the insertion site produces microorganisms, which may be accompanied by other infection symptoms, with or without bloodstream infection, any pain or tenderness or drainage, necrosis of the overlying skin at the VAD insertion site."

Mortality: Not included

Secondary outcomes

Thrombophlebitis: defined as "the incidence of phlebitis and the diagnostic criteria of phlebitis refer to the Infusion Therapy Standards of Practice."

Infiltration: defined as "whitening and edema with or without pain of the insertion site."

Catheter occlusion: defined as "occlusion means the disability of flushing the catheter without resistance and the ability to yield a blood return."

Limited Importance

Cost: Not included

Pain: Not included

Satisfaction: Not included

Catheters per participant: not included

Other outcomes reported in trial

Catheter failure: defined as "the incidence of any form of infusion therapy failure. Any form of infusion failure includes but is not limited to phlebitis, occlusion, infiltration, CRI, catheter damage, nerve injury, or accidental dislodgement."

Catheter dwell time: defined as "the period from the beginning of the catheterisation operation to the catheter was removed." - mean (SD)

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.value:
Approximately 75% of participants were receiving a continuous infusion 

CRBSI - defintion from trial registry.

characteristics.name: Outcomes
characteristics.value:
Critical Outcomes

CRBSI: defined as "bacteremia/fungemia with one positive blood culture obtained from a peripheral vein, clinical manifestations of infections (i.e., fever, chills, and/or hypotension), and no apparent source for the BSI except the catheter. One of the following should be present: a positive semiquantitative (>15 CFU/catheter segment) or quantitative (>103 Colony Forming Units/catheter segment catheter) culture whereby the same organism (species and antibiogram) is isolated from the catheter segment and peripheral blood; simultaneous quantitative blood cultures with a >5:1 ratio IV versus peripheral; differential period of IV culture versus peripheral blood culture positivity of >2 hours."

Primary BSI: Not included

Local Infection: defined according to CDC criteria - bacteremia or fungemia with at least one positive blood culture from a peripheral vein, clinical signs of infection, and no other apparent source for the bloodstream infection (BSI) except the device—regardless of whether the tip or entry site swab culture is positive.

Mortality: Not included

Important outcomes

Thrombophlebitis: defined as "≥ 2 of the following: pain, erythema, purulence, infiltration, palpable venous cord"

Infiltration: Reported 

Catheter occlusion: Reported

Limited importance

Cost: defined as "(calculations based on 20 minutes nursing or medical insertion time at relevant rates, plus the cost of the required equipment (cannula, insertion pack including dressing and solution, gloves, saline, syringe, extension tubing and starter pack for all plus fluid bag, tubing and secondary tubing for medication administration for those patients requiring this) for insertions, nursing time and equipment to routinely remove IVDs that were otherwise functional, and the costs of treating any complications that occurred (e.g., IVD-BSI)."

Pain: Not included

Satisfaction: Not included

characteristics.name: Outcomes
characteristics.value:
Critical outcomes

CRBSI: defined as "catheter-related bloodstream infection, defined as positive blood culture from a peripheral vein; clinical signs of infection (ie, fever, chills, or hypotension); no other apparent source for the bloodstream infection except the intravenous catheter (in situ within 48 h of the bloodstream infection); and a colonised intravenous catheter tip culture with the same organism as identified in the blood...Hospital costs were set at AU$25·13 for intravenous catheter plus administration set, burette, and fl uid bag; $21·83 for intravenous catheter plus admin istration set and fl uid bag; $12·73 for intravenous catheter plus end cap; and $0·37 gauze and tape for removal; and staff time (observed rates of 14·5 min per insertion and 4·5 min per removal at fixed industrial award wages for registered nurses of $32·93/h, junior [$45·96/h] and senior [$67·16/h] medical staff )."

Primary BSI: defined as "any positive blood culture drawn from a peripheral vein while an intravenous catheter is in situ or for 48 hours after removal"

Local Infection: defined as "organisms grown from purulent discharge or vein segment with no evidence of associated bloodstream infection."

Mortality: defined as "mortality with intravenous catheter in situ or within 48 h of removal, collected from hospital records."

Important outcomes

Thrombophlebitis: defined as ≥ 2 of the following: pain, erythema, swelling, purulent discharge, palpable venous cord

Infiltration: reported

Catheter occlusion: reported 

Limited importance

Cost: defined as "costs per patient for the course of intravenous therapy, based on equipment required for insertion and removal of intravenous catheters with prices from negotiated hospital supply contract rate."

Pain: not included

Satisfaction: not included

Catheters per participant: defined as "number of intravenous catheters needed per patient for the course of treatment."

Other outcomes reported in trial

Accidental removal: reported

Catheter failure: defined as "any premature removal of intravenous catheter before end of treatment, other than for routine replacement—includes phlebitis, infiltration, occlusion, accidental removal, and catheter-related bloodstream infections."

Catheter dwell time: defined as "overall duration of intravenous therapy (cumulative of all intravenous catheters) per patient (hours)."
